title_en: Tiantong Securities Co., Ltd. Liquidation Group v. Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd., Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd. Jinan Branch, Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd. Yantai Qingnian Road Sub-branch — dispute over return of deducted settlement funds
ruling_gist_en: 1. According to Article 139, Paragraph 1 of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 21 and 22 of the Administrative Measures on Customer Transaction Settlement Funds, a securities company has the management right over customer transaction settlement funds and also bears the responsibility to ensure the integrity of customer transaction settlement funds. For any act of infringement against customer transaction settlement funds, the securities company has the right and the obligation to claim relief. After a securities company is ordered to close and undergoes administrative liquidation, the administrative liquidation team established by the securities regulatory authority correspondingly acquires the rights and obligations of the securities company to ensure the integrity of customer transaction settlement funds.

full_text_en:
Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities Co., Ltd. v.  
Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd., Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd.  
Jinan Branch, and Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd.  
Yantai Qingnian Road Sub-branch  
— Dispute over Return of Deducted Settlement Funds  

【Ruling Summary】  

I. Pursuant to Article 139, Paragraph 1 of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 21 and 22 of the Measures for the Administration of Customer Trading Settlement Funds, a securities company has the right to manage customer trading settlement funds and is also obligated to ensure the integrity of such funds. Any infringement upon customer trading settlement funds may and shall be remedied by the securities company. When a securities company is ordered to be closed and undergoes administrative liquidation, the administrative liquidation group designated by the securities regulatory authority accordingly succeeds to the securities company's rights and obligations to ensure the integrity of customer trading settlement funds.  

II. Customer trading settlement funds serve to guarantee full delivery and payment with the counterparty to a securities transaction; therefore, such funds are subject to other priority rights, and their integrity must be ensured. Where a securities company owes a debt to the bank where the dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds managed by it is maintained, the bank may not directly deduct customer trading settlement funds from such account to realize its own claim.  

Supreme People's Court  
Civil Judgment  

(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 147  

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 248 Nandajie, Zhifu District, Yantai City, Shandong Province.  

Legal Representative: Jiang Xiyun, President of the Bank.  

Agent ad litem: Fu Weizhuang, lawyer of Shandong Xizheng Law Firm.  

Agent ad litem: Yang Meiling, lawyer of Shandong Xizheng Law Firm.  

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at 5/F, Qilu International Mansion, No. 180 Quancheng Road, Jinan City, Shandong Province.  

Person in Charge: Qian Wei, Deputy Head of the Liquidation Group.  

Agent ad litem: Zhu Wenting, male, of Han ethnicity, born on July 11, 1969, Deputy Head of the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities, residing at Room 1807, Building 10, Yangqiao Beili, Fengtai District, Beijing.  

Agent ad litem: Jiao Yue, male, of Han ethnicity, born on January 17, 1973, staff member of the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities, residing at Group 017, Gaolu No. 1 Community, Jianhua District, Qiqihar City, Heilongjiang Province.  

Defendant at First Instance: Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd. Jinan Branch, domiciled at No. 97 Jiefang Road, Lixia District, Jinan City, Shandong Province.  

Person in Charge: Qu Jia, Branch President.  

Agent ad litem: Fu Weizhuang, lawyer of Shandong Xizheng Law Firm.  

Agent ad litem: Yang Meiling, lawyer of Shandong Xizheng Law Firm.  

Defendant at First Instance: Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd. Yantai Qingnian Road Sub-branch, domiciled at No. 16 Qingnian Road, Zhifu District, Yantai City, Shandong Province.  

Person in Charge: Wang Na, Sub-branch President.  

Agent ad litem: Fu Weizhuang, lawyer of Shandong Xizheng Law Firm.  

Agent ad litem: Yang Meiling, lawyer of Shandong Xizheng Law Firm.  

The appellant, Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengfeng Bank), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2006) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 59 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court in the case of dispute over return of deducted settlement funds brought by the respondent, Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities), against the appellant and the defendants at first instance, Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd. Jinan Branch (hereinafter referred to as Hengfeng Bank Jinan Branch) and Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd. Yantai Qingnian Road Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Qingnian Road Sub-branch), appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Qian Xiaochen presiding as the chief judge, and acting judges Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu as members, to hear the case. Clerk Yuan Hongxia served as the court recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.  

The facts found by the Shandong High People's Court through trial are as follows:  

On June 27, 2003, Yantai Jinjian Property Management Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinjian Property) and Tiantong Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tiantong Securities) entered into a "Trusted Investment Management Contract," stipulating that Party A (Jinjian Property) entrusted Party B (Tiantong Securities) to manage assets consisting of government bonds with a market value of RMB 100 million for a term of one year. It was also agreed that Party B must guarantee the safety of all entrusted funds of Party A. Within three working days after the expiration of the trust period, Party B was to restore the assets entrusted by Party A for investment and deliver both the assets originally delivered by Party A for management and the income after deducting the management commission payable to Party B to Party A. This agreement was a renewal of the "Trusted Investment Management Contracts" signed on June 27, 2001 and June 27, 2002. The RMB 100 million funds entrusted by Jinjian Property for management were borrowed from Hengfeng Bank (formerly Yantai Housing Bank). On June 28, 2001, Jinjian Property instructed Hengfeng Bank to directly remit the RMB 100 million borrowed funds into the securities trading account opened by Jinjian Property at the Ji'an Road Securities Business Department of Tiantong Securities in Shanghai, with the customer name as Jinjian Property and account number 1001242709013314756.  

The Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities submitted three copies of the "Customer Securities Settlement Fund Custody Agreement" entered into respectively between the Jinan Jingqi Road Securities Business Department of Tiantong Securities and Hengfeng Bank Jinan Branch, between the Yantai Development Zone Changjiang Road Securities Business Department of Tiantong Securities and Qingnian Road Sub-branch, and between the Yantai Huanshan Road Securities Business Department of Tiantong Securities and Business Division III of Hengfeng Bank. Each agreement stipulated that the relevant subordinate institution of Hengfeng Bank would act as the custodian bank for Tiantong Securities, and Tiantong Securities would open a dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds at Hengfeng Bank for depositing customer trading settlement funds. The agreements respectively specified the account name and account number for the deposit accounts. The rights and obligations stipulated in the agreements provided that Party B (the custodian bank) undertook to make payments at any time in accordance with Party A's (Tiantong Securities) payment instructions during normal business hours; and that it would not use the funds in Party A's dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds for any other purpose. Any transfer of funds from the dedicated bank account for customer trading settlement funds into the bank's own account was deemed to be a direct misappropriation of customer trading settlement funds by the relevant custodian bank.  

After the term of the entrusted wealth management contract between Jinjian Property and Tiantong Securities expired, Tiantong Securities did not return the entrusted management funds as agreed, and the loan of RMB 100 million that Jinjian Property owed to Hengfeng Bank also remained unpaid. On January 18, 2005, Hengfeng Bank and Jinjian Property entered into a "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement," stipulating that Jinjian Property, in order to repay the principal and interest of the loan, transferred its RMB 100 million government bond margin held at Tiantong Securities to Hengfeng Bank, and Hengfeng Bank would assert the rights against Tiantong Securities. On February 5 of the same year, Jinjian Property notified Tiantong Securities in writing of the fact of the transfer of the RMB 100 million creditor's rights. On February 7 of the same year, Hengfeng Bank Jinan Branch deducted RMB 80 million from the dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds opened by the Jinan Jingqi Road Securities Business Department of Tiantong Securities at that branch; Qingnian Road Sub-branch deducted RMB 10 million from the dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds opened by the Yantai Changjiang Road Business Department of Tiantong Securities at that sub-branch. On May 22 of the same year, Qingnian Road Sub-branch deducted RMB 12 million from the dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds opened by the Yantai Changjiang Road Business Department of Tiantong Securities at that sub-branch. On the same day, Hengfeng Bank Jinan Branch returned RMB 2 million to the dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds of the Jingqi Road Business Department of Tiantong Securities. Thus, the two subordinate institutions of Hengfeng Bank actually deducted a total of RMB 100 million from the dedicated accounts for customer trading settlement funds opened by the two business departments of Tiantong Securities.  

After the court session, the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities submitted a "Prior Notice of Administrative Penalty and Order for Correction" issued by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, to prove that the CSRC had determined that the deduction by Hengfeng Bank was illegal and had imposed a penalty. Hengfeng Bank refused to appear in court for cross-examination.  

To seek recovery of the RMB 100 million of customer trading settlement funds and interest, the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities filed a lawsuit with the Shandong High People's Court, requesting that the court order Hengfeng Bank Jinan Branch and Qingnian Road Sub-branch to return the deducted RMB 100 million of customer trading settlement funds and interest, and that Hengfeng Bank bear joint and several liability.  

The Shandong High People's Court held that: After Hengfeng Bank acquired the creditor's right of Jinjian Property against Tiantong Securities for the RMB 100 million entrusted investment management, Hengfeng Bank replaced Jinjian Property as the creditor in the entrusted investment management relationship for the RMB 100 million management funds owed by Tiantong Securities. At the same time, its subordinate branches had signed customer trading settlement fund custody contracts with the subordinate business departments of Tiantong Securities, becoming the custodian banks in the custody relationship for customer trading settlement funds of Tiantong Securities. As a creditor, Hengfeng Bank had the right to demand that Tiantong Securities return the RMB 100 million funds it had entrusted for management; its subordinate branches, as custodian banks for securities customer trading settlement funds, were obliged to ensure the safety of the custody securities customer trading settlement funds. Because Tiantong Securities engaged in illegal operations and misappropriated the RMB 100 million entrusted wealth management funds for other purposes, resulting in its inability to return the RMB 100 million funds acquired by Hengfeng Bank on time, Hengfeng Bank had the right to assert its rights against Tiantong Securities in accordance with the law, and Tiantong Securities was obligated to return them. However, Hengfeng Bank, taking advantage of the special facility of its subordinate branches as custodian banks, forcibly deducted RMB 100 million from the dedicated deposit account for customer trading settlement funds of Tiantong Securities to repay the debt owed by Tiantong Securities, thereby infringing upon the interests of other securities customers. This is because the securities customer trading settlement funds in the dedicated deposit account deducted by Hengfeng Bank were not the property of Tiantong Securities, but were jointly owned by all securities customers, i.e., the settlement funds invested by customers in the securities market. Pursuant to the relevant provisions on the management of customer funds in the securities market, Tiantong Securities did not have ownership of the funds in the dedicated account for customer trading settlement funds jointly owned by securities customers. Even when Tiantong Securities went into bankruptcy liquidation, the funds in such dedicated account would not form part of the bankruptcy estate of Tiantong Securities. Hengfeng Bank argued that the RMB 100 million creditor's right it enjoyed was of the nature of a government bond margin. Even if that were the case, after Tiantong Securities entered into the administrative closure and liquidation process, its rights should be exercised in accordance with the corresponding provisions, and it could not be considered that the custodian bank had the right to unilaterally deduct the securities customer trading settlement funds held in custody. Therefore, the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities's request for the return of the deducted RMB 100 million was legally well-founded and should be supported. The RMB 100 million customer funds improperly deducted by the various branches of Hengfeng Bank were used to repay the RMB 100 million debt owed by Tiantong Securities to Hengfeng Bank, and the liability should be borne by Hengfeng Bank. Hengfeng Bank and its branches, as co-defendants in the lawsuit, should jointly bear the responsibility of returning RMB 100 million to the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities. In conclusion, the court, in accordance with Article 117 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and upon deliberation and decision by the Judicial Committee of the court, ruled: Hengfeng Bank, Hengfeng Bank Jinan Branch, and Qingnian Road Sub-branch shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, return RMB 100 million in customer trading settlement funds and interest during the period of occupation (calculated at the deposit interest rate of the dedicated account for securities customer trading settlement funds and the actual period of occupation) to the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities. If the monetary payment obligation is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The case acceptance fee of RMB 510,010 and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 500,000 shall be borne by Hengfeng Bank.  

Hengfeng Bank, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Shandong High People's Court, appealed to this Court on the following grounds:  

1. In the first instance, the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities, as the plaintiff, lacked standing to sue.  
2. Because the appellant was unable to protect its legitimate rights and interests through normal judicial remedies due to procedural violations by the court of first instance, the appellant was forced to exercise its right to take possession of property on February 22, 2005, and took possession of the government bond margin that rightfully belonged to it.  
3. Because the RMB 100 million funds were of a margin nature, the appellant's exercise of the right to take possession of property in accordance with the law was entirely reasonable and legal. Specific reasons: (1) Taking possession of funds is a common practice among banks to recover funds from defaulting customers. (2) Given that money is a fungible thing, the appellant's taking possession of the government bond margin was lawful.  
4. The Supreme People's Court had made relevant determinations in similar previous cases regarding government bond margins, etc. The case of the Liquidation Group of the China New Technology Venture Investment Company Closed by the People's Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as the Zhongchuang Liquidation Group) (appellant, defendant at first instance) v. Jinjian Company (respondent, plaintiff at first instance) regarding the return of securities trading margin, concluded by the Supreme People's Court in May 2003, is similar to the present case and is requested for reference.  
5. The findings and judgment of the court of first instance are contradictory. In its civil judgment (2006) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 59, the court of first instance held: "As a creditor, Hengfeng Bank has the right to demand that Tiantong Securities return the RMB 100 million funds it had entrusted for management; … because Tiantong Securities engaged in illegal operations and misappropriated the RMB 100 million entrusted wealth management funds for other purposes, resulting in its inability to return the RMB 100 million funds acquired by Hengfeng Bank on time, Hengfeng Bank has the right to assert its rights against Tiantong Securities in accordance with the law, and Tiantong Securities is obligated to return them." Yet ultimately, the Shandong High People's Court ruled that the appellant should return the RMB 100 million funds and interest during the period of occupation.  
6. The findings of the court of first instance were one-sided, evading the main issues, and were extremely unfair to the appellant. The court of first instance only one-sidedly emphasized the appellant's status as a custodian bank but ignored the appellant's identity as the owner of the RMB 100 million government bond margin.  
7. The application of Article 117 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China by the court of first instance to rule that the appellant return RMB 100 million to the respondent was an error in the application of law.  
8. The "Prior Notice of Administrative Penalty and Order for Correction" issued by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, submitted by the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities in the first instance, has no legal effect in accordance with the law.  

Request for the second instance: (1) Set aside the civil judgment (2006) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 59 made by the court of first instance and reject the claims of the respondent at first instance. (2) The costs of the appeal shall be borne by the respondent.  

The respondent, the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities, argued in response:  

1. When the appellant entered into the transfer of creditor's rights with Jinjian Property and implemented the deduction of Tiantong Securities' customer trading settlement funds, it neither notified Tiantong Securities nor asserted its rights before any judicial authority.  
2. The appellant's ground of appeal that the facts found by the court of first instance and the judgment result are contradictory is untenable. The appellant has confused two different legal relationships in this case: First, the creditor-debtor relationship arising from the appellant's acceptance of the creditor's rights transferred by Jinjian Property and consequently with Tiantong Securities. Second, the legal relationship combining tort and breach of contract arising from the appellant's violation of the "Customer Trading Settlement Fund Custody Agreement" signed between the parties and national laws and regulations by improperly deducting Tiantong Securities' customer trading settlement funds. The court of first instance did not err in its findings of fact and judgment results.  
3. The appellant's ground of appeal that the creditor's rights it accepted were of the nature of customer trading settlement funds is untenable. The RMB 100 million funds delivered by Jinjian Property to Tiantong Securities under the name of entrusted wealth management did not have the nature of customer trading settlement funds or so-called "government bond margin."  
4. The appellant does not have the right of recovery over the funds in Tiantong Securities' customer trading settlement fund account. Even if it were a "government bond margin" customer, the appellant had no right to exercise a deduction right over the funds in the dedicated deposit account for customer trading settlement funds.  
5. The national securities regulatory authority has clearly expressed its opinion that the appellant's deduction conduct was illegal and in violation of regulations.  

Request that the second instance dismiss the appeal and affirm the first instance judgment.  

This Court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance. In addition, this Court, through the second instance trial, further finds the following facts:  

1. On January 18, 2005, Hengfeng Bank (Party A) and Jinjian Property (Party B) signed a "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement," stipulating: (1) Party B transferred its RMB 100 million government bond margin (shareholder account B880125383) held at Tiantong Securities to Party A, thereby offsetting Party B's debt of RMB 100 million in principal owed to Party A; (2) Party B shall notify Tiantong Securities in writing that, from the date of signing this agreement, the creditor's right shall belong to Party A, and Party A shall assert the rights against Tiantong Securities.  
2. On March 17, 2006, the China Securities Regulatory Commission issued Administrative Penalty Decision No. [2006] 10, stating: In view of the fact that Tiantong Securities had misappropriated a relatively large amount of customer trading settlement funds and no longer met the conditions for continued operation, in accordance with Article 201 of the former Securities Law, it was decided to revoke Tiantong Securities' securities business license and order it to close. On the same day, the People's Government of Shandong Province issued Lu Zheng Zi [2006] No. 94, a "Letter on Entrusting Beijing Tianduo Law Firm to Conduct the Liquidation of Tiantong Securities Co., Ltd.," stating: In accordance with the spirit of the State Council's reply to the "Request for Instructions from the People's Government of Shandong Province, the People's Bank of China, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission on the Handling of Tiantong Securities Risks and the Restructuring of Qilu Securities," and the CSRC's penalty decision ordering Tiantong Securities to be closed and liquidated, the Shandong Provincial Government, after consultation with the CSRC, decided to entrust Beijing Tianduo Law Firm to conduct the liquidation of Tiantong Securities.  

This Court holds: Based on the appellant Hengfeng Bank's grounds of appeal and the respondent Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities's arguments in response, the focus of the dispute in this case is summarized as follows: First, whether the Liquidation Group of Tiantong Securities has the right to claim that Hengfeng Bank return the deducted securities trading settlement funds; second, whether Hengfeng Bank has the right to deduct funds from the customer securities trading settlement fund account managed by Tiantong Securities; third, the nature of the RMB 100 million funds entrusted by Jinjian Property to Tiantong Securities for management.

1. Regarding whether the Tiantong Securities Liquidation Group has the right to claim the securities transaction settlement funds deducted by Hengfeng Bank, i.e., whether the Tiantong Securities Liquidation Group is qualified as the plaintiff in this case. It is true that the client transaction settlement funds managed by Tiantong Securities do not belong to the company. However, Article 132 of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China, promulgated on July 1, 1999, and amended on August 28, 2004, provides: "Comprehensive securities companies must separately conduct their brokerage business and proprietary business, and their business personnel and financial accounts shall be separate, and mixed operations are prohibited. Clients' transaction settlement funds must be deposited in full with designated commercial banks and managed in separate accounts. Misappropriation of clients' transaction settlement funds is strictly prohibited." Article 212 of the same Law provides: "The implementation steps for the provisions of this Law concerning clients' transaction settlement funds shall be separately formulated by the State Council." Article 139, paragraph 1, of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China, amended on October 27, 2005, provides: "Clients' transaction settlement funds of a securities company shall be deposited in a commercial bank and managed in separate accounts in the name of each client. Specific measures and implementation steps shall be formulated by the State Council." Article 21 of the Administrative Measures for Clients' Transaction Settlement Funds provides: "When a securities company, a clearing company, a custodian bank, or a settlement bank encounters material abnormal circumstances in the dedicated deposit accounts for clients' transaction settlement funds, dedicated deposit accounts for clearing reserve funds, or capital verification special accounts upon the requirement of the China Securities Regulatory Commission or otherwise, it shall promptly report to the China Securities Regulatory Commission." Article 22 of the same Measures provides: "A securities company shall manage clients' transaction settlement funds in a centralized and unified manner. The clients' transaction settlement funds received by the subordinate securities business departments of a securities company shall, except for retaining sufficient funds for daily reserves, be handed over to the securities company for management." The above provisions indicate that a securities company has the right to manage clients' transaction settlement funds and simultaneously bears the responsibility to ensure the integrity of such funds. For any infringement of clients' transaction settlement funds, the securities company has the right and the responsibility to seek relief. Furthermore, in this case, paragraph 7 of Article 11 of the "Client Securities Settlement Funds Custody Agreement" signed between Tiantong Securities and Hengfeng Bank stipulates: "Any act of transferring funds from the bank dedicated deposit account for clients' transaction settlement funds into the bank's own account shall be deemed as the relevant custodian bank directly misappropriating the clients' transaction settlement funds." Therefore, Tiantong Securities also has the right to assert corresponding claims against Hengfeng Bank pursuant to this agreement. When a securities company is ordered to close and undergoes administrative liquidation, the administrative liquidation group established by the securities regulatory authority accordingly acquires the securities company's rights and responsibilities to ensure the integrity of clients' transaction settlement funds. Consequently, the Tiantong Securities Liquidation Group is a qualified plaintiff and has the right to file a lawsuit concerning the dispute in this case.

2. Regarding whether Hengfeng Bank has the right to deduct funds from the client securities transaction settlement fund account managed by Tiantong Securities. As acknowledged by the parties to the dispute, the account from which Hengfeng Bank deducted funds is the client securities transaction settlement fund account, and such funds belong to the clients of the relevant brokerage business. Apart from this attribute, the client securities transaction settlement funds also serve to ensure full delivery and settlement with the counterparties to securities transactions, meaning that other priority rights are attached to these funds, which is an important reason for maintaining the integrity of the client securities transaction settlement funds. Under the circumstances of this case, the right acquired by Hengfeng Bank from Jinjian Property, as stated in the "Debt Transfer Agreement" between the two, is sometimes referred to as the transfer of a RMB 100 million margin for treasury bonds, and at other times as the creditor's right of Jinjian Property against Tiantong Securities belonging to Party A (Hengfeng Bank), indicating that the nature of this right is unclear even to the parties themselves. In view of the current situation where Tiantong Securities has entered administrative disposition, through the identification and confirmation procedure, if this right constitutes client securities transaction settlement funds, it may be included in the scope of national acquisition, and there is no need to seek relief through litigation. If it does not constitute client securities transaction settlement funds, then this part of the right will become a creditor's right against Tiantong Securities, which can only be satisfied from Tiantong Securities' own assets and cannot be satisfied using the client transaction settlement funds belonging to the relevant clients. Judging from the content of the "Client Securities Settlement Funds Custody Agreement" signed between Tiantong Securities and Hengfeng Bank, Hengfeng Bank bears the obligation not to misappropriate such funds, and the agreement contains no provisions for exceptional circumstances. Hengfeng Bank shall maintain the integrity of the client securities transaction settlement funds in accordance with the agreement. Furthermore, other creditors in the same position as Hengfeng Bank, because they do not have access to Tiantong Securities' client securities transaction settlement fund account, cannot obtain satisfaction in the same way as Hengfeng Bank. Hengfeng Bank, by virtue of its position as the custodian bank for client securities transaction settlement funds, unilaterally deducted funds from the client securities transaction settlement fund account, which is unfair to the brokerage clients and other creditors of Tiantong Securities and also violates its agreement with Tiantong Securities. Based on the above reasons, whether Hengfeng Bank exercises or is able to exercise its right to claim repayment from Tiantong Securities cannot serve as a justification for Hengfeng Bank to deduct funds from the client securities transaction settlement funds. Therefore, this Court does not support Hengfeng Bank's claim that it has the right to retrieve the treasury bond margin belonging to it from Tiantong Securities' client securities transaction settlement fund account.

3. Regarding whether the RMB 100 million funds entrusted by Jinjian Property to Tiantong Securities for management have the nature of client securities transaction settlement funds. On March 17, 2006, the China Securities Regulatory Commission issued the Administrative Penalty Decision ([2006] No. 10), revoking Tiantong Securities' securities business license and ordering its closure. After entering the administrative disposition procedure, the identification of whether a client's right is of a creditor's right nature or a property right nature, i.e., whether it has the nature of client securities transaction settlement funds, involves the question of whether the state will acquire such right. In this regard, the People's Bank of China, the Ministry of Finance, the China Banking Regulatory Commission, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission jointly formulated and promulgated the "Opinions on the Acquisition of Individual Creditor's Rights and Client Securities Transaction Settlement Funds." The client transaction settlement funds determined by these Opinions to be within the scope of acquisition refer to: "Funds deposited by brokerage clients with securities companies to ensure full delivery and settlement, all proceeds from the sale of securities (minus brokerage commissions and other legitimate fees), dividends, cash dividends, and bond interest derived from holding securities, and interest on the above funds. Client securities transaction settlement funds that have been adjudicated by a court before the disposition of a financial institution and fall within the scope of acquisition." Regarding the identification and confirmation of whether funds constitute client securities transaction settlement funds, the Opinions state: "After identification and confirmation by the custodian group or liquidation group, an acquisition application for client securities transaction settlement funds shall be submitted, and upon approval by the regulatory authority, the acquisition payment shall be made concurrently with the implementation of third-party custody." In summary, with respect to whether a client's right constitutes client securities transaction settlement funds, after a securities company enters the administrative disposition procedure, the custodian group or liquidation group exercises the relevant identification authority, subject to approval by the regulatory authority. After Hengfeng Bank acquired the creditor's right from Jinjian Property, it should have requested identification and processing from the administrative liquidation group within the administrative disposition procedure of Tiantong Securities. However, regardless of whether this sum of funds constitutes securities transaction settlement funds, it does not constitute a legal basis for Hengfeng Bank to directly deduct funds from the client securities transaction settlement fund account managed by Tiantong Securities. Therefore, this Court does not make a determination on the nature of the above RMB 100 million funds.

In conclusion, the judgment of the first instance found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Pursuant to the provisions of Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment stands affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 510,010 shall be borne by Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Qian Xiaochen

Acting Judge: Liu Min
